independent_findings_and_remediation: A fastest-flow claim was not supported by user evidence; constrained the claim and added a measurable usability promotion gate.
Single-provider behavior needed a controlled creative-use path; retained multi-source promotion as the default and added a fail-closed owner-approved clean-room exception.
Sensitive questions could burden every user; personal-data, role, and payment details are conditionally disclosed.
A generated blueprint could be mistaken for change approval; implementation and deployment flags are immutable false defaults and approvals remain separate.
audit_checks: All retained sources are official HTTPS product pages.
The ledger asserts no copied code, visual design, or marketing copy and validation rejects such records.
A single-source exception requires rights PASS, scope-bound owner approval, original-expression exclusion, independent implementation, two distinctive additions, and similarity PASS.
Cosmetic-only changes are insufficient; two distinction categories and at least one workflow, accessibility, or domain-function improvement are required.
Ambiguous functional-distinction wording was remediated with category-specific pass/fail examples, evidence requirements, and a minimum owner-approval work order.
The implementation imports the existing PlatformBrief contract instead of bypassing the visual understanding flow.
The usability asset remains INDEPENDENT_IMPLEMENTATION until benchmark and owner approval.
post_remediation_checks: Focused launch and visual-dialogue tests: 23 PASS
remaining_risks: Real novice usability has not yet been measured; do not advertise the flow as fastest before the benchmark passes.
Official vendor pages can change; refresh and re-review the evidence ledger before a material pattern revision.
Rights review reduces but cannot eliminate intellectual-property uncertainty; ambiguous cases remain HOLD.
This PR exposes a domain bridge, not an automatically deployed public platform service.
